title: Recurrent Structural Policy Gradient for Partially Observable Mean Field Games
claim: A policy architecture consumes individual and aggregate state, and the mean-field update scheme that feeds it comes in two variants, exact and sampled.
layout: 3 panels: two stacked mean-field update panels left, architecture diagram right, dashed module boxes
description: The figure has three parts. On the left, two rounded boxes are stacked. Box A shows an analytic mean-field update: a blue gridded heatmap of μ(s1,s2) over axes s1 and s2, with an arrow labelled z to a second heatmap whose mass has spread and shifted. Box B shows the sample-based update: a scatter of blue points that is tightly clustered at first and more dispersed after the arrow labelled z. Both boxes carry |S| = |S1| x |S2| captions. On the right, panel C is the RSPG architecture. Blue arrows feed Individual State into a dashed Embedding block, and Shared Obs. of Aggregate State into a dashed RNN block with a recurrent loop. Both feed a dashed MLP block. The MLP outputs either Categorical Actions Logits or Continuous Actions, which are drawn as green stems showing log probability densities. A red arrow leads to Softmax for Categorical Distribution. The eye goes first to the blue heatmaps and scatter plots, then to the architecture.
caption: Top left: analytic mean-field updates compute exact expectations over next states. Bottom left: sample-based mean-field updates re-approximate the mean-field at each step. Right: RSPG architecture.
abstract: Mean Field Games (MFGs) provide a principled framework for modelling interactions in large population systems. However, algorithmic progress has been limited since model-free methods are high variance and exact methods scale poorly. Recent Hybrid Structural Methods (HSMs) reduce variance while maintaining tractability by leveraging low-dimensional individual state and action spaces and known transition dynamics to compute the exact expected return conditioned on Monte Carlo rollouts of common noise. However, HSMs have not been extended to partially observable settings. We propose Recurrent Structural Policy Gradient (RSPG), the first history-aware HSM for MFGs with public partial information. RSPG achieves an order-of-magnitude faster convergence than model-free RL methods while learning history-aware behaviour, unlike current HSMs. To facilitate research into MFGs, we also introduce MFAX, our JAX-based framework for MFGs that supports both analytic and sample-based mean-field updates. MFAX and usage examples can be found at https://clarisse-wibault.github.io/rspg/.
